title: ICAEW representation17/26
finding: Questions economic viability, remuneration of backing assets, competitive implications and rationale. These are questions about income earned on issuer backing assets, not a recommendation that holders should receive interest. Incorporates an earlier response but references REP015/24 despite describing Bank response; REP016/24 also separately read below.
provisional_qualitative_stance: No express holder-remuneration permission/prohibition in this5-page document. Incorporated REP015/24 not newly read in full here.
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

title: ICAEW REP016/24: systemic payment systems using stablecoins
finding: Warns that switching to unremunerated Bank reserves on becoming systemic could make an issuer relying on reserve income unviable. Balances viability against financial stability and monetary-policy concerns. This cannot establish support for paying reserve income to holders.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Issuer-reserve-income/viability concern; no express holder-remuneration stance found in entire8-page text.
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

title: Comment from Consumer Reports
date_note: Date from respondent primary announcement; PDF itself undated. Announcement: https://advocacy.consumerreports.org/press_release/consumer-reports-highlights-safeguards-needed-to-protect-consumers-from-stablecoin-risks-in-comment-letter-to-treasury-department/
finding: Consumer Reports criticizes low bank savings returns but opposes passive stablecoin rewards because of uninsured deposit substitution, credit tightening and faster runs. It distinguishes such returns from active user-directed DeFi participation and lending. Thus consumer advocacy cannot be treated as uniformly pro-remuneration.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Opposes passive holding rewards; would preserve active user-directed DeFi returns. No express safe-reserve-pass-through policy separately identified.
short_exact_excerpt: passive accrual of yield or interest on stablecoins / active participation in DeFi protocols or governance-related activities
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

title: Circle Internet Group, Inc.
finding: Circle supports an issuer-centred anti-evasion prohibition and opposes a de minimis exception, while protecting independent merchant incentives, distributors and customer rewards outside issuer direction. It rejects using reserve regulation to preserve banks’ deposit bases and expects little effect on lending. Its support for bounded non-remuneration draws on payment-product identity and competitive parity among issuers, without endorsing the bank-funding argument.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Issuer-paid/proxy yield prohibited; independent third-party rewards protected. This is not a recommendation for general issuer-to-holder reserve-income sharing.
short_exact_excerpt: The OCC should not replace the current framework with an overbroad blanket prohibition.
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

title: Coinbase Global, Inc.
finding: Coinbase rejects the OCC presumption and third-party expansion as exceeding statutory authority and reversing enforcement burdens. It expressly links permitted profit sharing to reserve earnings, defends ordinary distribution agreements and third-party rewards, and invokes consumer welfare/payment competition against wider restrictions.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Defends issuer-only statutory perimeter and third-party rewards. Statutory-restatement recommendation is not blanket permission for issuer interest.
short_exact_excerpt: Those profits, by definition, may reflect interest or yield on reserves.
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

title: American Bankers Association
finding: ABA asks for express direct/indirect prohibition, broader connected-party scope and scrutiny of reserve-income-funded distributor payments. Its economic case includes both lost deposits and compositional changes when retail funding returns as uninsured wholesale balances. Do not repeat its p15 description of the direction of the CEA numerical effect as an independently verified fact.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Supports broad prohibition including issuer-derived reserve income routed to holders.
short_exact_excerpt: Reserve interest flows from the issuer to the exchange, which may then pass some portion of that yield to retail users.
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

actor: Bank Policy Institute, Financial Services Forum, and Consumer Bankers Association
title: Bank Policy Institute, Financial Services Forum, and Consumer Bankers Association
finding: BPI/FSF/CBA prefer express prohibition over rebuttable presumption, broadly covering equivalent benefits. They explicitly discuss reserve interest re-labelled as distributor compensation; invoke credit intermediation and issuer margins/risk incentives; and request clear-and-convincing evidence for rebuttal. This is materially more restrictive than either Circle or Coinbase.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Supports broad direct/indirect prohibition, including reserve-income routing.
short_exact_excerpt: a PPSI uses interest it receives on reserve assets to compensate an affiliate or related third party
quantitative_action: None; frozen actor-episode dataset and heatmap unchanged. New qualitative supplement only.

title: Independent Community Bankers of America
pinpoint: Primary web PDF reader pp40–43; p1identity/date andopeningcontextpp2–5. Whole48-pagePDFnotretrieved as bytes.
finding: ICBA seeks broad direct/indirect prohibition without a de minimis exception. It identifies reserve-income distributions through a trust or special-purpose vehicle as evasive and would make the presumption irrebuttable for some arrangements. Its rationale joins community-bank credit, consumer protection and regulatory parity.
provisional_qualitative_stance: Broad prohibition; explicit reserve-income conduit example.
short_exact_excerpt: the issuer directs reserve income to a trust or special purpose vehicle that makes distributions to stablecoin holders
